Apps on Omnix · 18 apps tested

Decentralized app distribution.

Attestation and signing allow apps to be distributed through GitHub. A release carries a signed attestation that ties each binary to the source and the build that produced it, so you can verify an app without a central app store.

Every app here also comes with a workflow an agent runs in a booted NixOS VM: the real binary, the real commands, the real session. A status only appears after that test has run, and each card shows when it last ran and against which commit. Re-run the test after an update and the card tells you whether your workflow survived it.

OBS Studio 32.2.2

Recording and streaming

Patched

Screen recording and live streaming. Omnix ships nixpkgs' OBS with its own shutdown fix, carried on the Omnix-Linux/obs-studio fork.

Omnix-Linux/obs-studio fork · omnix/32.2.2 · GPL-2.0 · Website

Details
workflow an agent verifies
  1. Build Omnix's OBS: nixpkgs obs-studio 32.2.2 plus the fix from Omnix-Linux/obs-studio (omnix/32.2.2, commit 5218ef9), pinned by hash
  2. obs --version runs
  3. Start OBS in an X11 session; OpenGL loads (Mesa llvmpipe in the VM)
  4. The main window maps and OBS is still running 15 s later; take a screenshot
  5. Quit OBS through the window manager: it must exit with Result=success and leave no core dump
Test
Omnix-Linux/Omnix/tests/apps-gui.nixnix build github:Omnix-Linux/Omnix#checks.x86_64-linux.app-obs
Last run
Patched on 2026-10-06 at Omnix-Linux/Fresh NixOS VM run of Omnix's OBS. Upstream OBS can crash on exit when a preview, multiview or screenshot destructor runs after obs_shutdown() has freed the core; Omnix carries the fix (proposed upstream as obsproject/obs-studio#13906) on the Omnix-Linux/obs-studio fork and applies it in pkgs/obs-studio.nix (Omnix-Linux/Omnix#7). The test now quits OBS and requires a clean exit. The crash was a shutdown-order race, so a clean exit here shows the patched build shuts down correctly; it can't prove the race never occurs.

patching file frontend/widgets/OBSBasicPreview.cpp

programs.obs-studio.enable = true;   # now Omnix's patched OBS

OpenCut 0.3.0

Video editor

Passing

Open-source browser video editor (Next.js), built from its v0.3.0 source, served locally and opened in Brave.

GitHub source (tag) · v0.3.0 · MIT · Website

Details
workflow an agent verifies
  1. Fetch the OpenCut v0.3.0 source tag from GitHub (no Linux binary, AppImage, flake or nixpkgs package exists); bun dependencies pinned by output hash
  2. Build the Next.js app offline in Nix (next/font's Google Fonts download answered with Next's mock hook and the nixpkgs Inter font)
  3. Start OpenCut's own standalone server on 127.0.0.1:3000 with the upstream .env.example placeholders; /projects returns the app
  4. Open /editor in Brave's official Linux build in an X11 session (--no-sandbox as root, software GL via SwiftShader since the VM has no GPU)
  5. The editor creates a new project and redirects to /editor/<uuid>; the welcome dialog shows
  6. Dismiss it: the editor (assets, preview, properties, timeline) shows "Untitled Project"; take a screenshot
Test
Omnix-Linux/Omnix/tests/apps-opencut.nixnix build github:Omnix-Linux/Omnix#checks.x86_64-linux.app-opencut
Last run
Passing on 2026-10-06 at Omnix-Linux/Fresh NixOS VM run (nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.app-opencut) on the Omnix base with its desktop preset; the screenshot above is from this run. OpenCut publishes only the web app's source (its v0.3.0 release has no assets; nixpkgs has no package; no flake), so the test builds it from source. The editor's renderer needs WebGL2 or WebGPU: in the GPU-less VM Brave needs --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader, without which it shows "Failed to load project". The editor gates viewports under 1024 px, so the VM screen is 1280x800. Icon: OpenCut's own logo (apps/web/public/logos/opencut/icon.svg, MIT). Test in Omnix main (Omnix-Linux/Omnix#6).

Principles

How an app earns its place

  1. Tested, not claimed

    An app is listed for the workflow a test runs, not for a line in a feature list.

  2. Every status links to a test

    Passing, patched, known gap and failing all point at the NixOS test file and the commit it ran against. The page build refuses a status without one.

  3. Re-run after every update

    When Omnix, nixpkgs or the app changes, an agent re-runs the test and records the new result, so you can see whether a workflow that worked yesterday still works after the upgrade.

  4. Rollback when an update breaks one

    A failing workflow is a reason to stay on, or boot back to, the previous generation until it is fixed.

  5. Agent-maintained

    An agent adds an app by writing a test and a registry entry, running it, and recording the result. No hand-edited badges.

  6. No special packaging

    Apps run as unmodified upstream binaries through the Omnix standard filesystem layer: /lib64, /usr/lib, ldconfig and envfs.
